newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ford says Australia profits, imports a worry.
newsitem.headline: Ford says Australia profits, imports a worry.

text.p: Ford Motor Co's Australian subsidiary expressed concern on Tuesday about the local car-making industry's profitability and declining volume base.
Ford Australia president David Morgan, arguing against proposals for steep cuts to car import tariffs, said foreign-made vehicles were "coming over the wharves in frightening numbers".
Growth in new vehicle demand in Australia had been flat for nearly 20 years, yet imports had made major gains, he said.

"Six years ago imported cars accounted for barely 20 percent of new car sales. For the first quarter of this year, that figure had soared to a massive 55 percent," Morgan told a luncheon in Melbourne.
"In fact, more (are imported) every week than Korea imports in a year based on last year's figures," he added.

The car industry is lobbying against a proposal by the Productivity Commission to lower tariffs to five percent by 2004. Tariffs are scheduled already to fall from the current 22.5 percent to 15 percent by 2000.
Japanese car makers Mitsubishi Motors Australia Ltd and Toyota Motor Corp Australia both recently reported losses for their Australian operations.
